clue.text: Suppress ultimately scathing report

parts.note: to suppress something is to ban it

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word scathing

explanation.surface: A damning report is hushed up at the last.
explanation.definitionFit: A report can be a loud explosive noise, such as a gunshot, which is a synonym of bang.

clue.text: Detest a bore endlessly detaining husband

indicators.note: detaining means the shortened bore holds the next piece inside it
endlessly means the word bore loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before being cut

explanation.surface: Someone loathes a tedious person who keeps their husband talking forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts BORE to BOR, and 'detaining' puts H inside it to make BHOR, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to detest something is to loathe or abhor it.

clue.text: Get through using this code agent fashioned

indicators.note: fashioned means shaped anew, so the letters of this code agent are rearranged

explanation.surface: A spy builds a cipher to pass a message through enemy lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashioned' rearranges the thirteen letters of THIS CODE AGENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to go the distance is to last right to the end, to get through something.

clue.text: America backing competitor importing Vermont's No.1 relic

indicators.note: backing means the abbreviation for America is read backwards
importing means the word for competitor takes a letter inside it

parts.note: a competitor is a rival

indicators.note: No.1 picks the first letter of Vermont's

explanation.surface: An American rival brings in a historic artefact from Vermont.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns US into SU; 'importing' puts V (Vermont's No.1) into RIVAL, giving RVIVAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is something surviving from the past, which is one sense of a survival.

clue.text: Poor actor in South East — pity

indicators.note: in means the word for a poor actor goes inside the compass letters

parts.note: SE is the compass abbreviation for South East
a ham is an overacting, poor performer

explanation.surface: A bad performer in the south-east of England is to be pitied.
explanation.definitionFit: In 'what a pity', pity carries the same sense of regrettable misfortune as shame.

clue.text: Looking most embarrassed about nasty deeds? Right

indicators.note: about means the abbreviation for right goes around the other letters

parts.note: RT is an abbreviation for right, as in Rt Hon

indicators.note: nasty signals that the letters of deeds are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone blushes deepest after their wicked acts — rightly so?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' gives RT, as in Rt Hon. The surface makes 'about' mean 'concerning', but it is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Embarrassment makes the face flush, so the most embarrassed person is the most red in the face.

clue.text: Mark on page — upside-down butterfly?

parts.note: something upside-down has been inverted
the comma is a British butterfly named for a white comma-shaped mark on its wing

explanation.surface: A printed mark that looks like a butterfly turned over.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the butterfly is the comma species, so the upside-down insect is also, whimsically, the punctuation mark itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised, turned-over comma shape that opens a quotation is a punctuation mark seen on a page.

clue.text: Some coarse nickname that's toxic?

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A rude nickname is poisonous to the person called it.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenic is a classic poison, an example of something toxic.

clue.text: Island group quiet, and for French, secure

parts.note: SH is the call for quiet
ET is French for and
to secure something, such as a job or a fish, is to land it

explanation.surface: A cluster of islands is calm, and a French deal is clinched.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shetland Islands are an archipelago north of the Scottish mainland, an example of an island group.

clue.text: Check about son's underwear

indicators.note: about means the word for check wraps around the other letter

parts.note: to vet is to check
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A parent inspects a boy's undergarments.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a vest is a sleeveless undershirt, an item of underwear.

clue.text: This easy task in cold spell getting bravo for female

indicators.note: getting signals that the word for a cold spell takes a new letter
for says the new letter stands in place of the old one

parts.note: a freeze is a spell of icy weather
B is bravo in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An easy job done in a chilly spell earns a woman a cheer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting bravo for female' swaps the F of FREEZE for B.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is a breeze is very easy, an idiomatic term for a simple task.

clue.text: Book on island, good, important

explanation.surface: A book about an island is good and significant.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something big, as in a big decision, is important.

clue.text: Trip to deliver money after expression of hesitation

indicators.note: after places the word for money behind the hesitation sound

parts.note: er is the sound people make when hesitating
the rand is the currency of South Africa

explanation.surface: A courier makes a delivery run and gets paid after some dithering.
explanation.definitionFit: An errand is a short journey to deliver or collect something.

clue.text: Participate to one's profit, ancient ghetto being redeveloped?

indicators.note: being redeveloped signals that the letters of ancient ghetto are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Developers cash in by rebuilding an old district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being redeveloped' rearranges the letters of ANCIENT GHETTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to get in on the act is to join something so as to share in its benefits.

clue.text: Smashing iPods, extremely expensive incident

indicators.note: smashing breaks the letters apart so they can be reassembled
extremely picks the outermost letters of expensive

explanation.surface: Breaking costly music players is quite an event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives the two Es of 'expensive', and 'Smashing' mixes them with IPODS.
explanation.definitionFit: An episode is a single event or occurrence, a synonym of incident.

clue.text: Manage poem in Old English

indicators.note: in places the word for a poem inside the abbreviation

parts.note: verse is poetry, a poem

explanation.surface: An instruction to handle a poem written in Anglo-Saxon.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to oversee is to supervise or manage.

clue.text: Shoddy stuff that he initially rejected

indicators.note: rejected means a letter is thrown out of the word that
initially picks the first letter of he

explanation.surface: Rubbish that a man threw out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'he initially' is H, and 'rejected' removes it from THAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tat is British slang for cheap, tasteless goods or junk.

clue.text: Merit in struggle to overcome resistance by trade union

indicators.note: to overcome means the word for struggle goes over and around the next pieces

parts.note: to vie is to struggle or compete
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: There is merit in fighting to overcome opposition from a union.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a virtue is a good quality, a merit.

clue.text: Where is crease, Ken enquired tactfully first of all: near this

definitions.text: Where is crease, Ken enquired tactfully first of all: near this

indicators.note: first of all takes the opening letter of each of the six words before it

explanation.surface: Ken politely asks where the crease is, and is told it is near this.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the crease is a line marked near the wicket, the set of stumps the batter defends, so the whole question also points to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The batting crease in cricket is drawn close to the stumps, so the thing it lies near is the stumps.

clue.text: Sought favour of English in golf club

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for English inside the club

parts.note: a wood is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: An Englishman at the golf club tried to win someone over.
explanation.definitionFit: To woo is to court someone or seek their favour, so wooed is the past tense.

clue.text: In mid-term on northern street see painter Max

indicators.note: in mid-term takes the middle letters of the word term

explanation.surface: Halfway through the school term, look at a painter on a northern street.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Ernst was a German Surrealist and Dada painter.

clue.text: Twelve unchanged on reflection

definitions.note: twelve o'clock midday; the word itself is a palindrome

indicators.note: unchanged on reflection says the word reads the same when mirrored end to end

parts.note: twelve o'clock midday; the word itself is a palindrome

explanation.surface: The number twelve looks the same in a mirror.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday is twelve o'clock, so twelve stands for the middle of the day.

clue.text: Rage not, strangely, in NI Parliament

parts.note: to storm is to rage

indicators.note: strangely signals the letters of not are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: An appeal for calm in the Northern Ireland Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' rearranges NOT into ONT. Stormont is the Belfast seat of Northern Ireland's devolved parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Stormont is the building and common name for the Northern Ireland Assembly, so it stands for that legislature.

clue.text: Clergyman, King, always close

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex
ever means always
a close is an end

explanation.surface: A priest and a monarch are forever intimate.
explanation.definitionFit: A reverend is a member of the clergy, a minister.

clue.text: Opposed to European time frames

indicators.note: frames means the words European time hold the answer inside them

explanation.surface: Someone is hostile to continental time zones.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti as a preposition means against, so it is a synonym of opposed to.
